description:
prob gonna sell cemoto for ausom dt2 pro with @48v. Don #fyp #viral #cemoto #tuttio 
How to sell a Cemoto in exchange for an Ausom DT2 Pro with 48V: steps, negotiation tips, and safety checks. #cemoto #tuttio
Lead
Looking to trade a Cemoto for an Ausom DT2 Pro with a 48V system? This guide outlines how to prepare your Cemoto for sale or trade, what to check on the Ausom DT2 Pro, and practical tips to negotiate and complete the exchange safely.

Prepare your Cemoto for sale
- Clean and inspect: Wash the Cemoto and perform a visual inspection. Note any damage, missing parts, or recent repairs. Clear photos help support your asking terms. 
- Documentation: Gather title, service records, receipts, and any manuals. Having ownership documents ready speeds the transaction.
- Basic maintenance: Address small issues that reduce value — tighten bolts, top up fluids or battery, and fix lights if needed. Be transparent about known problems.

Evaluate the Ausom DT2 Pro (48V)
- Confirm specifications: Verify the Ausom DT2 Pro is the 48V model and confirm battery condition, range, and charger type.
- Inspect condition: Check frame, tires, brakes, electrical connections, display, and any included accessories.
- Test ride: If possible, test ride to confirm motor function, handling, and that the 48V system performs as advertised.

Negotiation and pricing
- Establish a baseline value: Research market prices for similar Cemoto models and for Ausom DT2 Pro 48V units. Use those figures to set a fair trade range.
- Consider value gaps: If the Ausom DT2 Pro has higher value, request cash on top or additional parts; if your Cemoto is worth more, expect the other party to add cash.
- Be clear on terms: Define what’s included (chargers, spare parts), who pays transfer fees, and whether any warranty applies.

Safe transaction steps
- Meet in public: Choose a safe, public location with good lighting and CCTV when possible.
- Verify identity and ownership: Ask to see ID and matching ownership documents; avoid transactions without proof.
- Payment method: Prefer cleared payment methods (bank transfer confirmation, cash in person). For trades plus cash, confirm funds before handing over the vehicle.
- Bill of sale: Draft a simple bill of sale outlining vehicles, VIN/serial numbers, agreed exchange, price adjustments, date, and signatures from both parties.

After the trade
- Transfer documentation: Complete title transfer and any registration steps promptly according to local rules.
- Change locks/keys: If applicable, secure your property by changing locks or removing personal tracking devices.

Closing / Call to action
Ready to proceed with selling your Cemoto for an Ausom DT2 Pro 48V? Use the checklist above to prepare both machines, agree clear terms, and prioritize safety. Share the details of your Cemoto’s condition and what you expect in trade to speed up negotiations.

description:
shi does not stop only thing that’s stopping me is the weight of the scooter ✌🏻#fyp #fypシ #viral #dt2pro #ausom 
Is the Ausom DT2 Pro's braking system a major issue? A rider shares their experience, saying the only thing stopping the scooter is its own weight. #dt2pro #ausom
For many riders, the feeling of speed is addictive, and it seems like the only thing that can bring them to a halt is the physical weight of the vehicle itself. This sentiment is perfectly captured by a rider of the Ausom DT2 Pro scooter, who humorously notes, "shi does not stop only thing that’s stopping me is the weight of the scooter."

The core of the issue is a complete lack of braking capability. As the rider points out, the scooter has "ZERO stopping power." This is a significant concern for any electric scooter, as effective brakes are essential for safety. The Ausom DT2 Pro, while perhaps known for its speed, appears to fall short in this critical area, leaving the rider to rely on the scooter's own mass to slow down—a potentially dangerous situation.

This review highlights a major flaw in the DT2 Pro's design. For anyone considering this model, the lack of stopping power is a serious point to consider. It raises questions about the scooter's overall safety and whether the thrill of speed is worth the risk of being unable to stop when needed.
